bearings.paper_claim: Against a passive opponent with known allocation w_b, the low-allocation optimum has a term linear in w_bi with common coefficient c = (Ba/Bb - 1): shadow the opponent's targets if Ba > Bb, avoid them if Ba < Bb (Eq 5, low-allocation limit only; a degree term enters only when positivity constraints bind). Continuous shadowing plus shielding is within 1.89e-3 of the numerical optimum under budget advantage (degree 2.09e-2, uniform 2.14e-2). Under disadvantage it is 7.28e-4 vs 2.12e-3 for discrete degree targeting (K=16, 15 instances).
bearings.paper_location: Results p.7 Eq 5 (text lines 414-470); pp.11-12 Fig 6 (text lines 711-734)
bearings.system_side: contested_bills.py docstring says no consumer exists today for the CONTESTED_V1 dial. The registry is display-only: build_dashboard_bundle.py lines 731-745 loads it and shows it in the posture block with consumer False, fed to no engine. build_opposition_prior.py lines 1528-1542 defines w_b as relational exposure (independent expenditures, communication costs and conduit money removed) summing to 1.0, labelled coalition-builder adversary substrate / shadowing layer. No fec/engine file or moneyball_core.py references it. The registry file contested_bills.json is not present in the repo root.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Design template only. w_b is relational FEC-associated exposure drawn from a sample of 10 companies per industry (build_opposition_prior.py line 108; not industry-complete), not LDA (D-021). The paper's dynamics are an unnoised voter model on one academic email network, so c and the gap sizes are not calibrated for Congress. The sign of the response needs the per-bill budget ratio measured first. UNVERIFIED for this system until a second path reproduces it (DE-062).
bearings.verifier_note: All quoted numbers reproduce from the text, including the Eq 5 coefficient and the Fig 6 gaps. Softened because Eq 5 is the low-allocation limit only and the degree term is omitted. The system_side phrase no code uses yet is too strong: the registry is loaded and displayed by build_dashboard_bundle.py. The citation of Romero Moreno 2021 inside the registry could not be found in the repo.

bearings.paper_claim: With a passive opponent the continuous optimum spreads widely: 111 of 1,133 nodes (H plus A) get above-average allocation and 1,013 nodes (V) are near flat with std/mean 0.11. Continuous optima beat the best discrete plan by 5-10 percent for passive K below 100 (Fig 1c, 15 samples). With two active controllers the unique pure-strategy Nash equilibrium is uniform targeting w_ai = Ba/N, reported as independent of network type and budgets (numerical result; the uniqueness proof is in S1 Appendix Section 12, not in the text file).
bearings.paper_location: Results p.5 Fig 1a (text lines 285-308); p.6 Fig 1c (text lines 337-345); p.13 Nash equilibrium (text lines 758-782)
bearings.system_side: optimize.py greedy spends a 2.5M pot in 500-dollar chunks with a 10k per-member cap (lines 24-27). Industry money ind = fm.ind0 is set once at line 59 and never rewritten, so industry is a frozen passive opponent. marg_at (lines 64-72) changes only the funded member's pflip. Conversion events call shift_pro (lines 93-105, 136-142), which rewrites that member's stance in MAT; the nA and nB camp totals in flip_model.topic_setup are rebuilt from MAT, so a conversion does move neighbours' pull.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's spread and shielding come from money propagating through the network's steady state. Melange's dollar term is node-local, so the paper's spread cannot arise from dollars alone; shielding-like behaviour can arise only through the b term of a/(a+b) and through conversion-driven stance moves. The Nash result implies the plan is a best response to a frozen opponent and is exploitable if industry re-optimises; qualitative only. Equal-budget and per-candidate FEC limits have no analogue in the paper.
bearings.verifier_note: The counts 111, 1,013 and std/mean 0.11, the 5-10 percent gain for K below 100, and the uniform Nash result reproduce from the text. Softened because the text gives |Z| as 9 at line 302 and 7 at line 307, which this bearing does not flag, and because the claim that CU dollars do not change neighbours' nA and nB omits the conversion channel through shift_pro.

bearings.paper_claim: Steady-state opinions solve (L + Wa + Wb) x = wa for the voter model with zealots (Eq 1 rate equation on p.3; Eq 2 vote share on p.4). In the high-allocation limit (w much larger than d) the optimal allocation has no degree dependence (Eqs 7-8, pp.7-8).
bearings.paper_location: Model pp.3-4 Eqs 1-2 (text lines 180-235); Results pp.7-8 Eqs 7-8 (text lines 480-540)
bearings.system_side: flip_model.py pflip (lines 92-97): a = WM*pm*saturating CU term + WP*nA/mAt, with b mirroring it using industry money and anti-camp neighbours, returning a/(a+b). It is a one-shot ratio, not a steady-state solve. Neighbour camps nA and nB are fixed by stance; mAt and mBt are maxima over nodes (lines 132-143).
bearings.transfer_conditions: The functional form is analogous (a share-of-pull ratio), but the paper's neighbour states are endogenous while Melange fixes them from stance, so the paper's HMF results do not transfer. Read pflip only as a vote-share proxy, never as a vote or access probability (D-025). The analogy itself is an inference (DE-062).
bearings.verifier_note: Equations and limits reproduce from the text. Eq 2 appears on p.4 rather than p.3. The code description matches flip_model.py lines 92-97.

bearings.paper_claim: The degree correlation of optimal allocations is a by-product of shielding: Kendall tau is generally above 0.5 for K above 30 for both optimal and pure-shielding plans (Fig 5b). When the passive controller targets nodes whose neighbours have the lowest degree, |tau| for optimal allocations falls below 0.25 while shielding gives tau down to about -0.5 (Fig 5c). The authors conclude that optimal allocations can be explained almost perfectly by shielding without degree preference (p.11).
bearings.paper_location: Results pp.10-11, Fig 5b-c (text lines 646-681); quoted sentence p.11 (text lines 680-681)
bearings.system_side: kb_benchmark.py computes Katz-Bonacich centrality on build_P and reports Spearman rho against the optimizer allocation (two variants), observed CU money, observed industry money and the legislative score. The docstring says nothing in the chain consumes it. Output goes to data/network/kb_benchmark.json.
bearings.transfer_conditions: An allocation-centrality correlation, high or low, can come from where the opponent places money rather than from a preference for centrality, so any reading of rho should be stratified by industry-money placement or labelled UNSTRATIFIED. Rho is a heuristic diagnostic, not closeness or influence evidence (D-025). The paper's evidence is one email network.
bearings.verifier_note: The tau thresholds and the quoted sentence reproduce from the text. The paper uses Kendall tau and the code uses Spearman rho, so the two statistics are not interchangeable and the comparison in the bearing is across statistics.

bearings.paper_claim: In the discrete regime optima are driven mainly by node degree (hub targeting). Shadowing and shielding matter mostly in the continuous regime, and shielding weakens as K grows (K = 256 in Fig 3c).
bearings.paper_location: Results pp.9-10 Fig 3c and Fig 4 (text lines 576-620); p.12 summary (text lines 737-755); Discussion p.13 (text lines 792-795)
bearings.system_side: budget_frontier.py cascade(): progressive two-colour first-to-reach spread from A and B seeds over the P kernel with edge-keyed CRN draws. Bystander activation uses min(0.9, ind/BSCALE) (line 133). MAXSEEDS defaults to 60 (line 7).
bearings.transfer_conditions: IC is progressive (an activated node stays activated) and the voter model is reversible, so only the regime point transfers: seed-set optimisers will tend toward hubs, and opponent-aware placement matters more when allocation is continuous. One network and no noise in the paper. The lazy-greedy description of the frontier engine was not checked in this pass.
bearings.verifier_note: The discrete-regime degree finding and the K = 256 shielding weakening reproduce from the text. The cascade, the 60-seed default and the bystander activation reproduce in budget_frontier.py. Lazy greedy was not verified.

summary_issues: Overall: no bearing is refuted. Verdicts are 2 softened (contested-bills, joint-optimizer) and 3 reproduced (flip-model, katz-bonacich, competitive-cascade). Coverage: text file read in full for the cited sections; S1 Appendix and figures not in the text file.

The registry citation claim (flags and summary) could not be verified. contested_bills.json is absent from the repo root, and no Moreno string appears in fec/lobbying or fec/tests/lobbying. Source it or remove it.

Summary says the registry cites this paper for a counterparty term that no code uses yet. More accurate: build_dashboard_bundle.py loads and displays the registry (display-only), and no engine consumes it.

Summary says money never spreads to neighbours so shielding cannot emerge. Dollars alone do not spread, but conversion events (optimize.py shift_pro) change a converted member's stance and therefore neighbours' camp totals. Restate it that way.
The |Z| count is inconsistent in the paper: 9 at text line 302 and 7 at line 307. The summary and flags carry this; the joint-optimizer bearing does not.
The std/mean 0.11 applies to the 1,013 near-flat V nodes, not to all allocations. The summary's remaining mass phrasing should say so.

gaps_exposed says a non-uniform opponent is most exploitable on low-degree nodes. Paper Eq 6 weights each node's deviation by 1/d_i, so misallocating low-degree nodes matters more; the controller is more exploitable when it neglects low-degree nodes.

w_b is described as approximating FEC opposition money. The code basis is relational associated exposure with independent expenditures, communication costs and conduit money removed, built on a sample of 10 companies per industry and not industry-complete (build_opposition_prior.py line 108).
paul_alignment cites Paul's margin note on Kim 2025 and his stance on the joint optimizer. paul_entries is empty and no annotations were read, so these attributions are unverified.
Eq 2 is on p.4 and Eqs 7-8 on pp.7-8; the rel's p.3 location for Eq 2 is off by one page.
The uniqueness of the Nash equilibrium and its independence from network and budgets rest on S1 Appendix Section 12, which is not in the text file. Only the numerical result was checked.
The katz-bonacich bearing sets the paper's Kendall tau beside the code's Spearman rho. Different statistics; the comparison should be labelled as such.
The lazy-greedy description of budget_frontier.py was not verified in this pass; only the cascade, the 60-seed default and the bystander activation were checked.
